design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that families completed baseline assessment and were then randomized to the EBFI, SBFI, or waitlist condition, although the sequence-generation method is not described.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was explicitly randomized after baseline assessment, but the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not reported; the groups were generally comparable, although child age and paternal criminal-history risk differed at baseline.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: families completed a 90-min semistructured interview, parent-report measures, and home-observation and then were randomized to conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and practitioners necessarily knew the behavioral program received, adherence among treated completers was high, but analyses were restricted to completers rather than intention-to-treat and 24 of 87 randomized families did not complete postassessment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 87 families eligible to participate in this evaluation, 63 (72%) completed intervention and postassessment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Postintervention outcome data were missing for 24 of 87 randomized families (28%), missingness was associated with baseline child-problem severity and interacted with condition for parenting conflict, and the complete-case analyses did not address potential missing-not-at-random bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A significant Condition Completer interaction was found for mothers’ reports of conflict over parenting on the PPC... Irrespective of condition, mothers who did not complete the intervention rated their child’s behavior on this measure as more problematic than those who did complete the program.

domain_judgments.rationale: The measures were established and applied consistently, and observational coders were blinded, but many key outcomes were mother-reported and mothers knew their assigned condition, making differential reporting plausible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All coders were blind to the intervention conditions of participants, stage of assessment, interactions used for reliability checks, and the specific hypotheses being tested.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and numerous eligible outcome scales, subscales, time points, ANCOVA/MANCOVA analyses, pairwise contrasts, and clinical-change definitions created scope for selective reporting, although the stated hypotheses and many null findings were presented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Short-term intervention effects were analyzed by a series of 3 Group (EBFI vs. SBFI vs. WL) MANCOVAs or ANCOVAs or both with preintervention scores as covariates and postintervention scores as dependent variables.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because 28% of randomized families lacked postintervention data, missingness was related to baseline outcome severity and parenting conflict, and analyses were complete-case rather than intention-to-treat. Additional concerns arise from unreported sequence concealment, unblinded parent-reported outcomes, and lack of a prespecified analysis plan.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that eligible families were randomly assigned to the enhanced self-directed, self-directed, or waitlist condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment was reported and demographic balance was assessed, but the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not described, and some baseline outcome means differed appreciably across the small groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Upon returning the completed assessment forms and meeting selection criteria, families were randomly assigned to either the enhanced self-directed (14 families), self-directed (15 families) or waitlist (12 families) group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew whether they received written materials, telephone support, or no treatment, and the single postassessment dropout appears to have been excluded rather than analyzed by intention to treat, although intervention delivery and fidelity procedures were otherwise clearly specified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One family, assigned to the ESD condition, did not complete the postassessment, meaning that 40 (98%) families completed pre and postassessment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Postintervention data were available for 40 of 41 randomized families (98%), and only one additional family was missing at follow-up, making material bias from missing outcomes unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: There was a very low level of attrition in the current study. One family, assigned to the ESD condition, did not complete the postassessment, meaning that 40 (98%) families completed pre and postassessment. One family, from the SD condition, did not complete the 6-month follow-up assessment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The main positive outcomes were reported by unblinded mothers who received the behavioral intervention and could therefore have been influenced by treatment expectations, while independent behavioral observations were absent and father reports did not show significant effects.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The results from the present study should be interpreted with caution as mothers’ observations and reports of child behaviour were unable to be confirmed by independent behavioural observations.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified analysis plan was reported, and numerous outcomes, subscales, reporters, time points, contrasts, and clinical-change analyses provided scope for selective reporting, although null findings were also presented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The parent-monitoring, parent-report and self report measures were completed by mothers and fathers in all three conditions at pre- and postintervention.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven primarily by reliance on unblinded maternal reports for the main favorable outcomes without independent observation, alongside null father-reported effects. Unreported randomization/concealment methods, lack of clear intention-to-treat analysis, and absence of a preregistered analysis plan add further concerns.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that consenting foster families/children were randomly assigned to wait-list control, brief PCIT, or extended PCIT conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment was explicit and baseline groups were mostly comparable, but the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not reported, and two caregiver characteristics differed at baseline.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Consenting families were randomly assigned to one of three study conditions... However, tests revealed two significant differences: Caregivers in the control group were more likely to be African American and they had been licensed as foster parents for a longer period of time.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew their assignment and the intervention included differential compensation, while adherence and unintended deviations were not fully reported; although the authors describe an ITT analysis, it excluded randomized participants without any post-baseline assessment and used LOCF.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Analyses for the present study included all subjects who completed a post-baseline assessment, resulting in an effective sample size of 75... All analyses were run in SAS 9.3 under intention-to-treat (ITT) assumptions, including the last observation carried forward (LOCF) method.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 75 of 102 randomized families entered the reported analyses and only 68 completed the final assessment, so substantial missingness—often from placement change or caregiver nonresponse—could plausibly bias outcomes despite similar attrition rates and LOCF imputation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Analyses for the present study included all subjects who completed a post-baseline assessment, resulting in an effective sample size of 75 and a retention rate of 73.5%. Seven families dropped out of the study after the second assessment, resulting in 68 completers of the third and final assessment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although validated measures were administered consistently, all reported outcomes were caregiver ratings and unblinded caregivers both received the behavioral intervention and assessed child symptoms, creating substantial potential for expectancy, demand, and social-desirability bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of chief concern is that parent raters were not blinded to study condition, which could introduce internal validity threats such as demand characteristics and social desirability bias.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, and several scales, time trends, omnibus tests, and pairwise contrasts were available, leaving scope for selective reporting despite identification of externalizing behavior as the primary outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Our principal interest in these analyses lies with tests of interactions between contrast-coded vectors representing the hypothesized treatment comparisons and linear and quadratic orthogonal polynomial trend contrasts representing time.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by substantial missing outcome data/exclusion of 27 randomized families and by unblinded caregiver-reported outcomes that were susceptible to expectancy and social-desirability effects. Unclear sequence concealment and lack of reported preregistration add further concerns.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports that 101 eligible families were randomized 1:1 to the HNC or TE-HNC parallel treatment arm.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although allocation was explicitly randomized 1:1 and no significant demographic baseline differences were reported, the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eligible families were then randomized 1:1 to either HNC or TE-HNC.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and therapists necessarily knew whether technology enhancements were provided, but intervention fidelity was high and the primary analyses appropriately included all available participants under intent-to-treat guidelines, with no reported intervention-related deviations likely to bias effects.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For primary group difference analyses, full information maximum likelihood (FIML) estimation techniques were used for inclusion of all available data based on intentto-treat guidelines.

domain_judgments.rationale: Retention was similar between groups, missingness showed no association with treatment or measured participant factors, the MCAR test was nonsignificant, and FIML/ multiple imputation were used to limit bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Further, random patterns of missingness along with a non-significant Little’s missing completely at random (MCAR) test, χ2(239) = 267.64, p > .05, suggest that the mechanism of missingness was MCAR and support use of multiple imputation and FIML for primary analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: The validated parent-reported and structured observational outcomes were measured consistently, but caregivers were unblinded and could influence parent-reported outcomes, while blinding of observational coders was not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At all waves caregivers completed the (ECBI; Eyberg & Robinson, 1983).

domain_judgments.rationale: A trial registration identifier and prespecified primary versus secondary outcome categories are reported, but the text does not establish prospective registration or provide a protocol/statistical analysis plan sufficient to exclude selection among multiple scales, follow-up contrasts, and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary outcomes were parent-reported and observed child behavior problems. Secondary outcomes included observed parenting skills use (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02191956).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. Missing-data handling and intervention fidelity were strong, but sequence generation/concealment were not described, subjective caregiver outcomes were assessed unblinded and observer blinding was unclear, and available reporting does not fully rule out selective result reporting.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports that eligible families were randomly assigned by Master's-level therapists to HNC or TE-HNC using restricted random assignment to force equal group sizes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Restricted random assignment was reported, but sequence generation and allocation concealment were not described, and the very small groups differed meaningfully in baseline disruptive-behavior intensity.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Using restricted random assignment to force equal sample sizes, Master’s-level therapists randomly assigned the remaining 22 eligible low-income families to the HNC or TE-HNC group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and treating therapists necessarily knew the assigned behavioral intervention, and the outcome analysis excluded randomized practice cases and dropouts rather than following intention-to-treat, although fidelity was high and therapists treated both groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Given the pilot nature of the project, we considered only complete data (i.e., data from participants available at pre- and post- treatment).

domain_judgments.rationale: Four of 19 analyzed randomized families (21%) lacked post-treatment data and were excluded, a substantial proportion in this very small trial, with insufficient evidence that missingness could not have biased intervention-effect estimates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Overall rate of attrition (21%) was substantially lower than what has been reported in prior BPT work with low-income samples.

domain_judgments.rationale: The child-behavior outcome was a validated measure applied in both groups, but it was reported by caregivers who knew their treatment assignment and directly experienced the additional smartphone support, making differential expectancy or reporting bias plausible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Intensity and Problem subscales on the 36-item ECBI (Eyberg & Pincus, 1999) served as the dependent measure of behavior change.

domain_judgments.rationale: A trial registration identifier is provided, but no protocol or prespecified analysis plan is presented for comparison, while multiple outcomes, subscales, effect-size approaches, and clinical-significance analyses allow potential selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Funding for this project was provided by NIMH 1R34MH082956 (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01367847).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by substantial complete-case attrition in a very small pilot trial and caregiver-reported outcomes from unblinded participants. Additional concerns arise from incompletely described allocation concealment, exclusion of randomized participants from analysis, and limited evidence about prespecification.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that 58 eligible families were randomly assigned after pretreatment assessment to GANA, standard PCIT, or treatment as usual.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although assignment was explicitly random and measured baseline demographics did not differ significantly, the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Families determined eligible by phone attended a 3- to 4-hr pretreatment assessment where parents provided written informed consent and were then randomly assigned to GANA (n = 21), PCIT (n = 19), or TAU (n = 18).

domain_judgments.rationale: The interventions were delivered with monitored fidelity and analyses were described as intention-to-treat, but families could not plausibly remain blinded during these distinct behavioral treatments, treatment completion was low, and the handling of missing posttreatment outcomes in the intention-to-treat analysis was not explained.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All results reflect intent-to-treat analyses (Higgins & Green, 2008).

domain_judgments.rationale: Posttreatment outcome assessments were available for 54 of 58 randomized families (93%), with no significant differential attrition by condition reported, so missing outcome data were limited.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Ninety-three percent (n = 54) completed posttreatment assessments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome instruments were established and observational coders were blinded, but many outcomes were parent-reported and parents necessarily became aware of treatment received, allowing knowledge or expectations to influence ratings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trained coders were blind to treatment condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, while numerous parent-report and observational outcomes and contrasts were analyzed, leaving scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We also conducted single degree of freedom contrast to compare the effectiveness of the three treatment conditions on each of the parent reported outcome measures at Time 2, controlling for the same outcome measure at Time 1.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns. The main issues are absent details on sequence generation and allocation concealment, unavoidable participant awareness for subjective parent-reported outcomes, incomplete explanation of the intention-to-treat handling, and no reported preregistration or analysis plan; missing outcome data were nevertheless limited and observational assessors were blinded.
